assets.prompt: Handheld smartphone photograph, shot at a slight upward angle, of a large rectangular pitch-side sponsor board standing at the edge of a football stadium at night under bright white floodlights. Printed on the pale off-white board in ONE single deep charcoal ink is a compound tournament mark lockup: a bold thick circular RING, and set around the inside of that ring the words CONTINENTAL CUP in a heavy condensed uppercase with small tight letter counters, and critically a THIN HAIRLINE RULE printed as a fine concentric circle separating the ring from the words, and a small simple central football device in the middle. The mark is one flat deep-charcoal ink on the pale board, no other colours. The floodlight falls unevenly so the LEFT and centre of the board are brightly and evenly lit while the RIGHT THIRD of the board face drops into soft shadow where the deep-charcoal ink and the pale board run close together in tonal value and the mark is hard to separate from the ground there. Realistic weathered outdoor board with faint scuffs and a slight sheen, casual real-world snapshot look, not a studio shot, no other logos or text anywhere on the board.

assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for last season's team-set trading card press PDF (flat, single record; to be converted to a live document and reverse-engineered into a merge template downstream).

Document: single trading card, 63.5 x 88.9 mm PORTRAIT (2.5 x 3.5 in), media box = trim, NO bleed box present (0 mm bleed), fonts fully embedded, produced from a genuine InDesign layout so convert_pdf_to_indd round-trips cleanly.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (reads like a bold full-bleed hero):
- Full-bleed near-black PITCH FIELD (#0B0E12) covering the whole card.
- The player PHOTOGRAPH fills the upper two thirds, knocked onto the dark field.
- PLAYER NAME across the lower third, large, in a heavy near-metallic display face, Floodlight Gold #E7B24C.
- SQUAD NUMBER very large, bottom-right corner, same gold display face.
- POSITION and CLUB LINE on one small condensed-sans line under the name, Card White #F4F1EA.
- SET YEAR small, bottom-left, Steel Rule #8A94A0.
- A thin Kit Crimson #B4232B rule separating the photo from the name band.
- The TOURNAMENT MARK, which the dark dramatic card leads the eye to expect large.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY BUILT (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The MARK is placed in a graphic frame only 9.5 x 9.5 mm, anchored TOP-LEFT, far smaller than the printed hero suggests. At the card's 600 dpi print resolution that frame is only about 224 x 224 px, so whatever mark art is bound must still read at ~9.5 mm.
- The mark frame is set to print REVERSED / knocked-out (mark art in Floodlight Gold or Card White) on the near-black field, NOT on the pale board the mark was photographed from. Polarity and ground are inherited, not chosen.
- The PHOTO frame is 52.0 x 74.0 mm (~1230 x 1748 px at 600 dpi); any placed photograph must reach that at native scale or it upscales soft.
- PLAYER_NAME, SQUAD_NUMBER, POSITION, CLUB_LINE and SET_YEAR are five separate text frames with their own object styles (they are NOT one flowing story), so the merge can map five text placeholders plus one photo frame plus one mark frame.
- NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however document_render_layout is called; bleed cannot be introduced into a PDF-derived template.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): PLAYER_NAME | SQUAD_NUMBER | POSITION | CLUB_LINE | SET_YEAR | PHOTO | MARK

Colours: Pitch Black #0B0E12 field, Floodlight Gold #E7B24C name and number, Card White #F4F1EA position/club, Steel Rule #8A94A0 set year, Kit Crimson #B4232B separator rule.

assets.defect_engineered: none engineered (honest spec) but load-bearing: it pins the trim, the 52.0 x 74.0 mm photo frame and 9.5 mm mark frame geometry, the 600 dpi proof resolution the licensing people sign off from, the squad-order requirement, and the per-player naming the partner distributes by; it also states the printer REQUIRES 3 mm bleed, which the supplied PDF physically cannot carry, forcing the bleed disclosure
assets.content:
CONTINENTAL CUP 2026 — CARD PRINTER SPEC (what we and the licensing partner need back)

TRIM & STOCK
- Card trim: 63.5 x 88.9 mm portrait (2.5 x 3.5 in), the same as last season's team-set file.
- BLEED: we require 3 mm bleed on all four sides on the press-ready file. Note: last season's PDF was supplied with no bleed box; if you build off it, tell us plainly what can and cannot be done about bleed.
- Print resolution: 600 dpi at trim. A full card at trim is therefore 1500 x 2100 px.

FRAMES (as we hold the geometry; confirm against the converted document)
- PHOTO frame: 52.0 x 74.0 mm, i.e. about 1230 x 1748 px at 600 dpi. Placed photography must reach this at native scale. Do NOT upscale to fill it — a soft interpolated card is a reject.
- MARK frame: 9.5 x 9.5 mm, top-left, i.e. about 224 x 224 px at 600 dpi. The mark prints reversed on the dark field. It has to still read as our mark at that size.
- Text: player name, squad number, position, club line, set year are five separate fields.

ORDER
- The press file runs the WHOLE STOCKED SQUAD, one player per page, in SQUAD-NUMBER ORDER (1, 2, 3 ... ascending). The roster export is not in that order. Do not ship it in the order it arrived.

PROOFS
- Proofs for licensing sign-off must be rendered at 600 dpi at trim (1500 x 2100 px), embedded density set. A screen-scale page raster is not a proof.

PER-PLAYER FILES (the partner distributes these individually)
- One single-card PDF per stocked player, named: CUP26_<squadnumber-2digit>_<Surname>.pdf (e.g. CUP26_07_Ferraz.pdf, CUP26_09_Okoye.pdf). The name on the file MUST be the player on the card inside it — the partner keys distribution off the filename, so a mislabelled file ships to the wrong channel.

DELIVERY
- One ordered multi-page press file, eighteen named single-card files, the proofs, and a note of anything about this spec the supplied file cannot meet.
